d: The Avatar Inspect Menu allows users to view other users' avatars, try on items, make purchases.
h:
The Avatar Inspect Menu allows users to view another user's Roblox avatar character, try on items, and even make purchases within a game. Roblox enables this menu by default and users in your game can access this menu in three ways:

  • Opening the game's main menu and clicking the View button next to a user in the Players tab.
  • Clicking on a user's name in the player list.
  • Selecting the Inspect option in the Avatar Context Menu, an opt-in feature which provides additional user-to-user social interaction.

You can customize a user's Avatar Inspect Menu in the following ways:

  • Change the inspect target from the user's Roblox avatar to their current in-game appearance.
  • Change the inspect target to a specific User ID, even if they are not in the game.

For more specific catalog access, you can also use the Avatar Editor Service to access and make changes to a user's platform-wide avatar within a game.

Inspect currently equipped items

By default, the Inspect Menu shows the same information as the user's Roblox Avatar profile page. The avatar outfit may not match the user's current appearance, since you may have opted to equip different accessories or avatar items at that specific moment.

In the cases where the default Inspect Menu may not be accurate to the current character's outfit, you can inspect a character's current outfit with the following steps:

  1. Disable the default profile-based Inspect Menu by setting GuiService:SetInspectMenuEnabled() with a value of false.
  2. Get a current HumanoidDescription from the target player character.
  3. Call GuiService:InspectPlayerFromHumanoidDescription() to load the Inspect menu based off of the HumanoidDescription.

Use the following code sample to inspect the currently equipped items of a specific player:

local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

-- Make profile-based Inspect Menu inaccessible
GuiService:SetInspectMenuEnabled(false)

local humanoid = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid")
if humanoid then
    -- Get current HumanoidDescription from a player character
    local humanoidDescription = humanoid:GetAppliedDescription()

    -- Load the inspect menu from a humanoid description
    GuiService:InspectPlayerFromHumanoidDescription(humanoidDescription, player.Name)
end

Inspect specific users

The Avatar Inspect Menu can inspect players who aren't in the current game. You can use GuiService:InspectPlayerFromUserId() to inspect a player from any Player.UserId.

Use the following code sample to open the Avatar Inspect Menu based on a UserId:

local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- Get user ID by username
local success, userId = pcall(function()
    return Players:GetUserIdFromNameAsync("RobloxUser")
end)

if success then
    GuiService:InspectPlayerFromUserId(userId)
end

kid.simple: The Avatar Inspect Menu lets players look closely at someone else's avatar, try on their items, and even buy them. It is on by default in every game. This page shows how to make the menu show what a player is wearing in your game right now, and how to open the menu for any user, even someone not in the server.
kid.analogy: It is like asking a friend where they got their cool jacket and then trying it on in the store mirror.
keyPoints: Players open the menu from the Players tab in the Roblox menu, by clicking a name in the player list, or from the Avatar Context Menu.
By default it shows the avatar from the player's Roblox profile, which might not match their look in your game.
To show their in-game look, turn off the default with `GuiService:SetInspectMenuEnabled(false)`.
Then get their current look with `humanoid:GetAppliedDescription()` and open it with `GuiService:InspectPlayerFromHumanoidDescription()`.
Use `GuiService:InspectPlayerFromUserId()` to inspect any user by their user ID, even if they are not in your game.

terms.inspect: Look closely at an avatar to see each item it is wearing.
terms.HumanoidDescription: An object listing everything about how a character looks, like clothes, accessories, and body colors.
terms.user ID: The number that identifies a Roblox account.
terms.profile avatar: The look a player set on their Roblox account, outside any game.
terms.pcall: Runs a function safely and catches errors, so a failed web request does not crash your script.

example.title: Open the inspect menu for a user by name
example.code:
local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- Look up a user ID from a username (this asks Roblox's servers)
local success, userId = pcall(function()
	return Players:GetUserIdFromNameAsync("Roblox")
end)

if success then
	-- Show the inspect menu for that user
	GuiService:InspectPlayerFromUserId(userId)
else
	warn("Could not find that user")
end
explain: `GetUserIdFromNameAsync()` turns a username into a user ID by asking Roblox online.
We wrap it in `pcall` because web requests can fail, for example if the name does not exist.
If it worked, `InspectPlayerFromUserId()` opens the inspect menu on that player's screen.

watchOut: Expecting the default menu to show in-game costumes. It shows the profile avatar unless you use `InspectPlayerFromHumanoidDescription()`.
Calling `GetUserIdFromNameAsync()` without `pcall`. If the name is wrong, the script errors and stops.
